notice: Engram is a third-party MIT program (Gentleman-Programming/engram). PiCode ships its engine unchanged: the name and logo are its author's trademarks, so no surface here is dressed as their product.
note: The pinned memory engine, fetched from its own release by build/engram-runtime.sh and carried at `<pack>/resources/memory/engram.exe`. Pinned, never `latest`: an editor built today must behave the same in six months, and the store it writes is shared with whatever other agent on the machine points at `~/.engram` — a version that moves on its own is a version that can migrate somebody else's memory without asking. 3.5.1 is the release the owner already runs, so PiCode joins the store it has rather than opening a second one on it. It is deliberately NOT the `gentle-engram` pi package: that package carries hooks, a status bar and session-identity machinery that this product removed with gentle-ai, and `left-behind-packages.ts` keeps an import from bringing it back. The protocol is written here instead.
